Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage overnight and today is dominated by the stunning Democratic sweep of Congress in the 2026 midterms and its market fallout, with CVS Health's major corporate breakup and Elon Musk's political and stock-market setback in Texas as the other big storylines. Outlets are also tracking how a Democratic-controlled Congress could reshape scrutiny of AI data centers, tech billionaires, and corporate America more broadly.

stories.headline: Democrats sweep Congress in a landslide rebuke of Trump
stories.summary: Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress in what multiple outlets describe as a historic rout of Republicans, with Trump himself acknowledging that the Iran war hurt the GOP; Politico and CNBC report Democrats even flipped long-red Texas statewide seats for the first time since 1994.

stories.headline: Stocks, bonds and gold rally as Wall Street cheers divided government
stories.summary: Global markets swung from overnight losses to gains after Trump accepted the midterm results, with Treasury yields and the dollar falling and gold surging above $4,000 an ounce on bets that divided government will limit fiscal risk-taking; CNBC noted Dow futures jumped roughly 800 points.

stories.headline: CVS Health to split into two public companies
stories.summary: CVS Health announced plans to separate its roughly 9,000 retail pharmacies from its insurance and pharmacy-benefit-manager businesses by early 2028, unwinding its $78 billion Aetna acquisition and ending the vertically integrated model it built since 2018.

stories.headline: Musk's record $474 million election bet backfires as Tesla, SpaceX shares slide
stories.summary: Elon Musk, the cycle's largest political donor, saw his favored Texas candidates lose badly while Tesla and SpaceX shares dropped roughly 4-7% in premarket trading, raising fears that Democratic control could bring tougher scrutiny of his companies' federal contracts and Texas operations.

stories.headline: Democratic wins threaten to slow the AI data-center boom
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that Democratic victories, especially Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's push for a data-center moratorium, could create fresh political and permitting obstacles for the AI buildout, with CNBC noting investigations into AI executives are already being called for by House Democrats.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco profit surges despite war-related disruptions
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco's profit rose on higher crude volumes and refined-product prices, offering relief to the kingdom's finances even as facilities face wartime pressures, according to WSJ and a separate Economist analysis.

stories.headline: Disney to lay off several thousand employees
stories.summary: Disney is planning several thousand job cuts and has asked some managers to reduce costs by as much as 20%, per CNBC's reporting.

Business.gaps: No recent business-relevant items were found for The Information or Puck; Washington Post, Forbes, Fortune, and Axios content was limited mostly to midterm-market reaction and Musk coverage rather than distinct lead stories.

US politics.overview: Nearly every outlet in this group is leading with the same story: a historic Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterms that flipped both chambers of Congress and several deep-red states, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Trump. Coverage is converging on the scale of the 'blue wave,' Texas's dramatic flip, looming Democratic investigations of the Trump administration, and the string of historic firsts among winning candidates.

stories.headline: Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress in historic midterm rout
stories.summary: Axios reports Democrats are projected to win at least 257 House seats to Republicans' 178 and at least 54 Senate seats, a landslide that exceeded even the most bullish pre-election forecasts and will usher in two years of investigations and legislative gridlock for Trump.

stories.headline: Texas turns blue for the first time in decades
stories.summary: Politico reports Democrats seized Texas after Republicans had run the country's second most-populous state for 30 years, with Gina Hinojosa winning the governorship and James Talarico defeating Ken Paxton for Senate, marking the first Texas Democrat elected to the chamber since 1988.

stories.headline: Democrats signal wave of investigations and subpoenas against Trump
stories.summary: RealClearPolitics notes Democrats in the House and Senate will gain subpoena power in January to investigate Trump and his administration on multiple fronts, a sentiment echoed by Sen. Ed Markey's "Subpoenas" post and incoming Oversight chair Robert Garcia's call to "lawyer up."

stories.headline: Trump accepts results, blames Iran war partly for GOP losses
stories.summary: WSJ reports Trump acknowledged the Iran war contributed to Republican losses as Democrats took Congress, while separately saying the U.S. plans to cut off military aid to Israel by year's end.

stories.headline: Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black House speaker
stories.summary: NPR reports that as speaker, Jeffries would be second in the presidential line of succession and has vowed to focus on affordability and holding the administration accountable.

stories.headline: Democrats set to win majority of U.S. governorships for first time in 16 years
stories.summary: Stateline reports Democrats are poised to control the majority of governors' offices after the GOP suffered major losses nationwide, including historic firsts such as the nation's first Black woman governor and first Native American woman governor.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump DOJ bid to intervene in California ballot dispute
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports the Court declined to intervene in California's ballot dispute just before Election Day, denying a last-ditch Trump administration effort, with more voting-related battles potentially ahead.

stories.headline: Voters nationwide reject data center buildouts in local elections
stories.summary: Stateline reports that 33 local ballot measures to restrict data center construction passed Tuesday night, reflecting widespread voter backlash against the AI infrastructure boom.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no fresh midterm-results coverage available; its most recent relevant piece predates election night. Politico, NYT, WSJ, and The Guardian coverage is limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's US midterms, where Democrats' sweeping wins are seen as a referendum on AI-driven data-center expansion and Musk's political spending, alongside Anthropic's blockbuster but risk-laden IPO filing. Outlets are also converging on Canva's mass layoffs, fresh details on the record $6.3B Binance hack tied to North Korea, and Google's new AI-vs-search tradeoff for schools.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep seen as rebuke of AI data-center buildout and Musk's political spending
stories.summary: Democrats retook the House and Senate partly by running against AI data centers and tech oligarchy, with Politico and Stratechery noting the result favors hyperscalers' regulatory environment in some ways but signals aggressive AI oversight ahead, while Elon Musk's roughly $446 million in midterm spending on favored candidates largely failed. The Information separately reported that Democrats rode a 'blue wave' with data centers explicitly on the ballot, and 404 Media framed the vote as a rejection of Silicon Valley's AI-powered political project.

stories.headline: AI labs stand up 'war rooms' to fight election disinformation
stories.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies set up special teams to monitor and counter disinformation efforts around Tuesday's US midterm elections. Platformer's Casey Newton examined whether this 'old playbook' for the deepfake era is actually working.

stories.headline: Canva cuts 22% of staff in its 'hardest year' amid slowing growth
stories.summary: Canva is laying off more than 1,200 employees, about 22% of its workforce, as the design platform faces what it calls its toughest year yet; The Information reported the cuts come amid worries that AI-generated visuals will erode Canva's market. The Register noted the company didn't explicitly blame AI but alluded to the pace of technological change.

stories.headline: North Korean hackers used fake job interview to pull off record $6.3B Binance heist
stories.summary: New details show North Korean operatives used a bogus job interview and an AI tool to breach Binance in the largest crypto heist on record, despite years of researcher warnings about these exact tactics. The Register reported Binance's own statement that it was 'not a single isolated breach,' while The Information noted the exchange says it has since rebuilt affected systems.

stories.headline: Google lets schools turn off AI tools, but only if they give up search too
stories.summary: Google will allow schools to disable AI features in its education products starting in 2027, but doing so also means losing access to standard search, a bundling move drawing scrutiny. The Decoder and The Information both flagged that AI will be off by default for schools, leaving administrators to opt in.

stories.headline: OpenAI hires former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security and government ties
stories.summary: OpenAI has hired Dan Driscoll, the former civilian head of the US Army, as 'Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization,' a move seen as aimed at winning government contracts and shaping AI policy. The Information noted Driscoll resigned his Army post in September before returning to the private sector.

stories.headline: Anthropic previews 'FlashProve,' an open-source system to cryptographically verify which AI model generated an output
stories.summary: In a company research post, Anthropic described FlashProve, an experimental open-source prototype for 'provable inference' that lets anyone cryptographically confirm an AI response actually came from the model it claims to be from, including guarding against labs secretly swapping in cheaper models. TechCrunch reported the system is still in research stages with no current plans for deployment at Anthropic or elsewhere.

Tech & AI.gaps: Rest of World and Google DeepMind had no recent AI/tech coverage found in search results within the allowed outlets for this period.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's US midterms, which flipped the House and delivered wins for clean-energy-friendly candidates and regulators, alongside continuing fallout from the Iran conflict's effect on oil markets and Gulf energy giants. Trade and specialist outlets (Heatmap, Latitude Media, Utility Dive) are also zeroing in on data-center driven grid strain, utility earnings, and the fate of federal permitting reform, while Carbon Brief looks ahead to the COP31 summit in Antalya.

stories.headline: Democrats Retake the House, Setting Up Energy Policy Fights
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that Democrats, after an election widely seen as a referendum on Trump, are planning to push to restore renewable tax credits, investigate DOE funding cuts, and scrutinize offshore wind and data-center policy now that they control the House.

stories.headline: Democrats Win Control of Georgia's Energy Regulator
stories.summary: Heatmap notes Democrats gained a third seat on Georgia's Public Service Commission in the midterms, a race that centered on rising utility bills and could shift the state toward more scrutiny of utility-data center deals and faster solar deployment.

stories.headline: Iran Turns to Guerrilla Tactics to Disrupt Strait of Hormuz Oil Flows
stories.summary: WSJ reports Tehran is using rocket-propelled grenades and limpet mines in an attempt to disrupt the restored flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf, keeping energy markets on edge.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco Profit Surges Despite War
stories.summary: The Economist and WSJ both report that higher oil prices have more than offset the impact of bombed facilities, with Aramco's profit boost attributed to higher crude volumes and stronger refined-product prices.

stories.headline: Data Center Demand Forecasts Could Cost Ratepayers Up to $624 Billion
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that grid operators' demand forecasts are running roughly 63 gigawatts above a more conservative baseline, with analysts warning the forecasting gap could saddle ratepayers with between $79 billion and $624 billion in unnecessary capital costs.

stories.headline: PJM's Revised Data Center Backstop Procurement Plan Shrinks Sharply
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports the planned procurement could fall to as little as 630 MW, down from an initial 6,800-MW target, after utilities in PJM's footprint lowered their large-load forecasts.

stories.headline: Energy CEOs Say Disruption Is the New Normal
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that top executives speaking at a major Middle East energy conference said companies must build backup capacity and diversify supply routes because disruption is no longer a rare 'black swan' event but a permanent planning factor.

stories.headline: 2026 Set to Rank Among Warmest Years on Record
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis finds that with three-quarters of 2026 complete, it is virtually certain the year will rank as the warmest or second-warmest on record, as the UK's climate minister warns that the upcoming COP31 talks must respond to alarming new science.

Energy.gaps: Could not independently verify current E&E News or Argus Media homepage leads via web search within these 48 hours; E&E News results returned mostly older archived pieces, so recent E&E coverage is not represented. Reuters, FT, and NYT block search, so only their provided feed items (on midterms/markets) were used.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across outlets this cycle centers on Beijing's efforts to prop up a slumping stock market and economy, the fallout from China's AI-stocks correction, new frontier AI model releases from Tencent and DeepSeek, and escalating China-Taiwan security friction alongside a Uyghur extradition case in Thailand.

stories.headline: China's central bank taps liquidity tool to aid struggling stocks
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China said it would conduct swap operations that could inject over $15 billion into equity markets after the CSI300 posted its worst month since 2016, as regulators move to shore up investor confidence following a sharp tech-stock correction.

stories.headline: China's AI stock-market struggles are a warning
stories.summary: The Economist examines what happens as China's supply of new AI technology begins to outpace market demand, framing it as a cautionary signal after a rocky month for Chinese tech equities.

stories.headline: China October NEV retail sales fall 10% to 1.148 million
stories.summary: Preliminary CPCA data show China's passenger new-energy-vehicle retail sales dropped 10% year-on-year in October even as the NEV penetration rate hit a record 67.8%, highlighting cooling demand despite rising market share.

stories.headline: China seeks arrest of five Uyghurs held in Thailand
stories.summary: Thailand's security chief said five Uyghurs detained since 2014 are subject to Chinese arrest warrants, with a Thai court to decide whether they will be handed over to Beijing, reviving concerns about forced repatriation.

stories.headline: Heightened Chinese activity detected near Taiwan
stories.summary: Taipei reported an uptick in Chinese military activity around Taiwan, part of a steady drumbeat of coverage this week on cross-strait tensions, live-fire drills in Kinmen, and defense budget deliberations.

stories.headline: Tencent launches Hy4 with vision and computer-use capabilities
stories.summary: Tencent released its Hy4 flagship AI model with new visual understanding and computer-use features, including the ability to interpret charts and documents and reason across multiple images, marking a capability leap among open-weight models.

stories.headline: Hong Kong records GDP rise of over 5% in first three quarters
stories.summary: Hong Kong posted GDP growth of more than 5% in the third quarter of 2026, extending the territory's strongest nine-month growth performance in five years.

China.gaps: Could not retrieve recent, topic-relevant coverage from Sixth Tone, Rest of World, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, or Yicai Global within the search allowance; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, and WSJ block search so only feed items (none provided for this group) could be used, and none were available for this beat.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Israeli/Palestinian outlets are dominated by two intertwined storylines: Israel's post-election turmoil as Netanyahu disputes the vote amid coalition talks, and the regional fallout from the US midterms, layered on top of the still-unresolved US-Iran war disrupting Gulf shipping and aviation. Gulf business outlets are separately tracking Saudi Aramco's strong Q3 earnings and a wave of UAE corporate deals even as the conflict weighs on regional economies.

stories.headline: Israel faces constitutional crisis as Netanyahu challenges election result
stories.summary: A constitutional crisis is brewing in Israel as caretaker PM Netanyahu, whose bloc won only 53 of 120 seats, escalates efforts to cast doubt on the election outcome, prompting Israel's attorney general to publicly rebuke the Shin Bet chief for trying to question Arab lawmakers without evidence.

stories.headline: Trump says U.S. plans to cut off military aid to Israel by end of year
stories.summary: Trump said Washington would end its $3.8 billion annual security assistance to Israel, a commitment that forms part of a 10-year agreement originally due to run through 2028.

stories.headline: Iran war disruption continues as attacks hit Hormuz shipping and Saudi targets
stories.summary: Regional tensions remain elevated with Saudi Arabia intercepting drones and a Houthi-launched ballistic missile, while Iran reported tankers damaged by mines near the Strait of Hormuz; WSJ separately reports Tehran is using guerrilla tactics like limpet mines to disrupt oil flows out of the Gulf.

stories.headline: Iran and Israel grapple with fallout from US midterms
stories.summary: Al-Monitor reports Iranian officials celebrated the Democrats' sweeping midterm win as a rebuke of Trump's Iran war, while separate Al-Monitor and Jerusalem Post pieces describe Netanyahu's rivals seizing on the result to push for his ouster.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco Q3 profit jumps 35% despite war disruption
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported a 35% rise in third-quarter net profit, helped by higher oil prices and the sale of a stake in a Malaysian refining firm, even as the company cut capital spending amid seven months of Iran war disruption.

stories.headline: Lebanon PM warns Hezbollah against joining another war
stories.summary: Asharq Al-Awsat reports Lebanon's prime minister cautioned Hezbollah against being drawn into a renewed conflict, as regional tensions tied to the Iran war remain high.

stories.headline: Emaar plans full takeover of Dubai-listed property unit
stories.summary: Emaar Properties is seeking full ownership of its Dubai-listed development subsidiary through a cash offer to minority shareholders, consolidating control of one of the UAE's largest residential developers.

stories.headline: UN candidate Lana Nusseibeh says Sudan's RSF must answer for 'atrocities'
stories.summary: The National reports that UN Security Council candidate Lana Nusseibeh said Sudan's RSF paramilitary force must be held accountable for atrocities committed during the ongoing civil war.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent distinct coverage found for Arab News, Ynetnews, Haaretz, Saudi Gazette, Zawya, Arabian Business, The New Arab, or Al Arabiya English within the last 24-48 hours; Al Arabiya English search results were outdated. Iran International's front page was current but focused on older protest-crackdown and execution stories rather than fresh developments.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by South Africa's November 4 municipal elections, seen as a referendum on the ANC's declining dominance and a test of a fragmenting opposition, alongside fallout from South Africa's exclusion from the US AGOA trade program. Business-focused outlets are converging on discussions from the Africa Financial Summit in Luanda about unlocking Africa's savings for private investment, while security and governance stories from Uganda, Niger/Libya and Nigeria's ruling party also feature prominently.

stories.headline: South Africans vote in tense municipal elections seen as test for ANC
stories.summary: South Africans voted Wednesday in local elections for councils in all 257 municipalities, with the ANC projected to remain the largest party nationally but facing further erosion of support and tough coalition talks in cities like Johannesburg where the DA's Helen Zille is a mayoral contender.

stories.headline: Opposition organiser killed as political violence mars South Africa election
stories.summary: Police are investigating the killing of an MK Party coordinator amid a wave of political violence, with authorities reporting 20 murders of political representatives and supporters during the municipal election period and more than 500 soldiers deployed to KwaZulu-Natal.

stories.headline: South Africa says US shifted goalposts on AGOA exclusion
stories.summary: South Africa's government said it is unfortunate that the reasons given for excluding it from the AGOA trade agreement did not match the conditions set during negotiations, while Rwanda is said to be less affected by the exclusion.

stories.headline: Africa has $4 trillion in savings, so why isn't it reaching businesses?
stories.summary: At the Africa Financial Summit in Luanda, policymakers and financiers examined why credit to the private sector remains thin even though African banks are among the most profitable in the world, with the IFC separately outlining plans to use cash-flow data to extend fintech lending to small businesses.

stories.headline: Madagascar teams with Gemcorp to raise $5bn for energy and mining
stories.summary: Madagascar is seeking to raise up to $5 billion by partnering with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island, according to a Bloomberg report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Five power battles inside Nigeria's ruling APC threaten Tinubu's 2027 bid
stories.summary: With Nigeria's opposition divided, the piece argues President Bola Tinubu's biggest political threats ahead of the 2027 election may come from internal APC rivalries rather than external challengers.

stories.headline: Inside Uganda's crackdown on online critics
stories.summary: The report examines allegations from Ugandan online critics of abductions and intimidation, with families searching for relatives who have gone missing after criticizing the government.

stories.headline: Niger signs cooperation deal with military leader in eastern Libya
stories.summary: Niger's prime minister approved an agreement during a visit to Benghazi to expand cooperation in multiple fields with Libya's eastern military leadership.

Africa.gaps: No recent Africa-specific coverage could be verified from Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT or WSJ, as these outlets block search and no relevant items were supplied in the feed.

Media.overview: Media-industry outlets are dominated by the fallout from the 2026 U.S. midterms, especially how cable news covered a historic Democratic sweep and Trump's public blaming of Fox News, alongside a fast-moving set of publisher-vs-AI stories (new opt-out tools from the big AI labs, Meta's new terms for UK publishers, and fresh lawsuits). Trade press is also tracking the ongoing Skydance consolidation of CBS News and CNN and the rise of prediction markets like Kalshi as an election-night news source.

stories.headline: Trump Blames Fox News as Cable News Grapples With Historic Midterm Losses
stories.summary: President Trump publicly faulted Fox News for the GOP's sweeping midterm defeats and said he would become a 'political pundit' on why candidates won and lost, kicking off wall-to-wall coverage of how networks handled a historic Democratic sweep.

stories.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft Team Up on a Publisher Opt-Out Tool
stories.summary: The four AI giants announced a joint standard that will let publishers block their crawlers in one step instead of having to opt out of each company's scraping individually.

stories.headline: Meta Accused of 'Holding Publishers Over a Barrel' Over New Terms
stories.summary: The News Media Association's chief executive urged the UK government to back the competition watchdog in pushing back on Meta's new terms for publishers, calling the platform's leverage unfair.

stories.headline: Publisher Lawsuits Against AI Firms Keep Piling Up
stories.summary: A new round-up shows U.S. newspapers suing Brave Software and Canadian publishers suing Anthropic, part of a widening global wave of publisher litigation and licensing deals with AI companies.

stories.headline: New York Times Adds 420,000 Subscribers as Q3 Digital Revenue Rises
stories.summary: The Times reported strong digital subscriber growth and said it expects digital-only subscription revenue to climb further in the fourth quarter.

stories.headline: Skydance Consolidation Keeps CBS News and CNN Leadership in Limbo
stories.summary: As Skydance prepares a company-wide voluntary buyout ahead of layoffs, Puck reports lingering uncertainty over who will ultimately run CBS News and CNN, with CBS alumni continuing to criticize Bari Weiss and David Ellison's direction of the networks.

stories.headline: Prediction Markets Like Kalshi Emerge as an Election-Night News Source
stories.summary: CJR interviewed Kalshi's CEO about betting markets becoming a fixture of midterm coverage, a theme Puck also explored in examining how much of Kalshi's business is actually driven by sports versus political wagers.

stories.headline: Judge Rules Against 'Famous Man' but ITN/Guardian Injunction Stays Pending Appeal
stories.summary: A court ruled against an unnamed public figure seeking to block an ITN/Guardian story about alleged abuse of power, though the injunction remains in place while he appeals.

Media.gaps: FT, WSJ, The Guardian and Bloomberg block web search and had no relevant feed items provided, so no recent media-industry coverage from them could be confirmed.
